glossary.au fond: at the back, at the end
glossary.aux: to the / at the / with (à + les)
glossary.bout: end (au bout de = at the end of)
glossary.c'est pour offrir: it's a gift, it's to give
glossary.ce sera tout: that's all / will that be all? (in a shop)
glossary.d'une: of a, by one (d'une heure = by an hour)
glossary.dès: from, as soon as (dès que possible)
glossary.enchantée: nice to meet you (said by a woman)
glossary.fait: does / makes / done, made / comes to
glossary.faut: (il faut) you have to, you need
glossary.fond: back, bottom (au fond = at the back)
glossary.installez-vous: have a seat, make yourself comfortable (vous)
glossary.j'ai mal: it hurts, I have a pain (j'ai mal à = my … hurts)
glossary.j'aimes: like (wrong form: aimes goes with tu)
glossary.j'arrive: I'm coming, I'm on my way / I arrive
glossary.j'arrives: am coming (wrong form: arrives goes with tu)
glossary.j'en: I … some, of it / of them
glossary.je descends: I'm coming down / I get off
glossary.je me suis trompée: I got it wrong, went the wrong way (said by a woman)
glossary.je sais pas: * I don't know (je ne sais pas)
glossary.jusqu'au: until the, as far as the
glossary.mal: bad / badly / pain (avoir mal = to hurt)
glossary.normal: normal, OK (ce n'est pas normal = that's not right)
glossary.normalement: normally, should (if all goes to plan)
glossary.occuper: to take care of, to keep busy
glossary.on est combien: how many of us are there?
glossary.on peut se tutoyer: can we say tu to each other?
glossary.on se voit: shall we meet? / we'll see each other
glossary.place: place, seat, room (à la place = instead)
glossary.quatres: four (wrong form: quatre never takes an s)
glossary.question: question
glossary.rapporte: bring back, take back / brings back
glossary.rattrape: make up (je, il; on se rattrape = we'll make up for it)
glossary.remet: puts back (on remet ça = let's do it another time)
glossary.soin: care (prendre soin de = take care of)
glossary.t'attend: waits for you, is waiting for you
glossary.trompé: got it wrong (said by a man)
glossary.télétravail: remote work (en télétravail = working from home)
glossary.va: goes / go! (tu) / is going to / is doing / suits
glossary.voilà: here is / here you are / there you go
glossary.à clé: with a key (fermé à clé = locked)
glossary.à droite: on the right, to the right
glossary.à gauche: on the left, to the left
glossary.ça marche: * OK, that works / does that work?
glossary.ça te va: does that suit you? / it suits you (tu)
glossary.ça va: how are you? / I'm fine / it's fine
glossary.ça va mieux: I'm feeling better / are you feeling better?
glossary.ça vous va: does that suit you? / it suits you (vous)

dialogues.cue: Léa, your flatmate, texts you. She says tu to you.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: Léa
turns.text: Demain, il y a grève. Pas de métro !

choices: There's a strike tomorrow: no metro
drills.miss: Reread: « il y a grève. Pas de métro ! »

drills.prompt: Say oh no, and that you'll go to the office by bike.
drills.model: Oh non ! Je vais au bureau à vélo.

dialogues.followUp: Bonne idée ! Moi, je reste à la maison.

dialogues.cue: A neighbour from the flat below rings at your door. She says vous to you. You're a woman.

turns.speaker: server
turns.text: Bonjour ! L'eau coule de mon plafond !

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Désolée ! Il y a ___ fuite dans la cuisine.

why: « Des » is plural. One leak: « une fuite ».

choices: Water is coming under her door
Water is coming through her ceiling
drills.miss: Reread: « L'eau coule de mon plafond ! »

dialogues.followUp: Vite, s'il vous plaît ! Ça coule beaucoup !

dialogues.cue: Mme Dumas, your landlady, writes on WhatsApp: she's late for your appointment. She says vous to you. Reassure her.

choices: Ouais, pas grave, à tout à l'heure !
Pas de problème, madame, je vous attends.
why: Good spoken French, but « t'inquiète » and « je t'attends » are for friends. Mme Dumas says vous to you.
« Ouais » is too casual for your landlady. She says vous to you.

dialogues.cue: You walk into the pharmacy opposite your building. The pharmacist says vous to you.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Bonjour, vous avez quelque chose contre la toux ?

turns.speaker: server
turns.text: Oui, bien sûr. Vous avez de la fièvre ?

drills.miss: Reread: « Vous avez de la fièvre ? »

drills.prompt: Say no, just a little cold.

dialogues.cue: You're at the hairdresser's. The hairdresser says vous to you.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Oui, mais ___ trop court, s'il vous plaît !

why: « Ne » needs a verb after it. Without a verb, say « pas trop court ».
Not French here: say « pas trop court ».

choices: If she can cut a little
drills.miss: Reread: « Je peux couper un peu ? »

dialogues.cue: You text Léa, your flatmate. She says tu to you.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: J'ai perdu mes clés, et le porte est fermée à clé.

drills.prompt: Tap the wrong word and fix it.

dialogues.cue: M. Ferrand, your neighbour, says vous to you. You had invited him to dinner tonight, and you've just told him you can't. You're a woman.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: M. Ferrand
turns.text: Vous avez un empêchement, madame ? Le dîner est annulé ?

why: « Désolées » is plural: you're one person.

dialogues.followUp: Ce n'est pas grave. Une autre fois !

dialogues.cue: Léa, your flatmate, texts you from work. She says tu to you.

turns.speaker: server
turns.name: Léa
turns.text: Tu es encore malade ? Je rentre à midi.

drills.prompt: Say yes: you're staying in bed today.
drills.model: Oui, je reste au lit aujourd'hui.

dialogues.followUp: D'accord. Je t'apporte de la soupe !

dialogues.cue: Léa, your flatmate, says tu to you. Which French word means “car-share”?

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Pas de train, alors je prends un ___ avec Théo ce matin.
